Series::bernoulli_¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series& Series::bernoulli_() const
Series& Series::bernoulli_(double p) const

What It Does¶

Overwrites every element of the receiver with an independent 0 or 1 — a single coin flip per element, with shared success probability p. The no-argument form uses p = 0.5.

p is one shared probability for the whole call. It is not read from the receiver’s current values — those are simply discarded. (The non-mutating bernoulli does support a per-element probability Series; bernoulli_ does not.)

Like the other in-place samplers, the receiver supplies the shape, dtype, platform, and storage. The 0/1 outcomes are then cast to the receiver’s dtype, so bernoulli_ accepts integer and Bool receivers as well as floating-point — only complex is rejected.

Reproducibility¶

Deterministic given the process-wide RNG seed. Call pluss::rng_seed(seed) before sampling to fix the outcomes; two runs from the same seed produce equal tensors. Each call advances a stream counter.

Parameters¶

p (double, default 0.5): the probability of drawing 1. Must be finite and in [0, 1]. p = 0 fills with zeros; p = 1 fills with ones — both deterministic.

Returns¶

Series& A reference to the receiver, now holding the outcomes. The write is in-place and preserves storage identity — every alias sees the values.

Raises¶

  • if the receiver’s dtype is complex

  • if p is non-finite or outside [0, 1]

Gradient¶

Not differentiable — there is no derivative with respect to p, and the overwrite discards whatever the receiver held before.

Examples¶

Example 1. Default p = 0.5. Seeded, so the flips are fixed.

pluss::rng_seed(42);
auto x = pluss::series::empty({10}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
x.bernoulli_();
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x);

Output¶

Series(shape=[10], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=10, contiguous=true)
data=[0.0000, 1.0000, 1.0000, 1.0000, 0.0000, 0.0000, 0.0000, 0.0000, 0.0000, 1.0000]

Example 2. p is a shared probability, not read from the buffer. p = 1 and p = 0 are deterministic fills.

auto a = pluss::make_series({9.0, 9.0, 9.0}); a.bernoulli_(1.0);
auto b = pluss::make_series({9.0, 9.0, 9.0}); b.bernoulli_(0.0);
std::cout << "p=1: "; pluss::series::print(std::cout, a);
std::cout << "p=0: "; pluss::series::print(std::cout, b);

Output¶

p=1: Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1.0000, 1.0000, 1.0000]p=0: Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.0000, 0.0000, 0.0000]

The 9.0s were ignored — bernoulli_ does not treat them as probabilities.

Example 3. Over a large sample, the fraction of ones converges to p.

pluss::rng_seed(7);
auto x = pluss::series::empty({200000}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
x.bernoulli_(0.3);
std::cout << "mean~" << x.mean().host<double>()[0] << "  (p = 0.3)\n";

Output¶

mean~0.301235  (p = 0.3)

Example 4. Integer and Bool receivers work too — the outcomes are cast to the receiver dtype.

auto i = pluss::series::empty({6}, pluss::ScalarType::Int32); i.bernoulli_(1.0);
auto bl = pluss::series::empty({6}, pluss::ScalarType::Bool); bl.bernoulli_(1.0);
std::cout << "int32: "; pluss::series::print(std::cout, i);
std::cout << "bool:  "; pluss::series::print(std::cout, bl);

Output¶

int32: Series(shape=[6], strides=[1], dtype=int32, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1]bool:  Series(shape=[6], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[true, true, true, true, true, true]

This is a difference from normal_ / uniform_, which require a floating (or complex) dtype.

Example 5. A complex receiver, and a p outside [0, 1], are rejected.

try {
  auto c = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Complex64);
  c.bernoulli_(0.5);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}
try {
  auto f = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
  f.bernoulli_(1.5);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

bernoulli_: complex receivers are not supported
bernoulli_: expected a finite probability in [0, 1]

Example 6. Reproducible under a fixed seed, and visible through aliases.

pluss::rng_seed(3);
auto a = pluss::series::empty({8}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64); a.bernoulli_(0.5);
pluss::rng_seed(3);
auto b = pluss::series::empty({8}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
auto alias = b;
b.bernoulli_(0.5);
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "a == b: " << a.equal(b)
          << "  alias.is_set_to(b): " << alias.is_set_to(b) << "\n";

Output¶

a == b: true  alias.is_set_to(b): true

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • p is one shared probability, not “read probabilities from this Series”. For a per-element probability tensor, use the non-mutating bernoulli.

  • Accepts integer and Bool receivers (unlike the continuous samplers); only complex is rejected.

  • p < 0, p > 1, NaN, and infinity are rejected.

  • Reproducible only after pluss::rng_seed(seed); each call advances the stream.

  • Not differentiable.

Summary¶

bernoulli_(p = 0.5) fills the receiver in place with independent 0/1 outcomes at shared probability p:

  • p is one number for the whole call, not read from the buffer

  • outcomes cast to the receiver dtype — integer, Bool, or floating; not complex

  • reproducible under pluss::rng_seed(seed); each call advances the stream

  • not differentiable; aliases see the write

See Also¶

  • Series::bernoulli: the non-mutating form, which also accepts a per-element probability Series.

  • Series::random_: uniform integers over an arbitrary range.

  • Series::geometric_: the count of trials up to the first success — repeated Bernoulli trials.

  • Series::uniform_: the continuous [0, 1) fill bernoulli_ thresholds internally.
